changes.review: PR #6: citation resolution and ibid state are output-affecting; run a full relink.
PR #5 after #6: Hebrew-numeral line markers are output-affecting; run a full relink.

PR #6 and PR #5 with the ibid checkpoint sidecar: the sidecar itself is output-neutral (an uninterrupted book sees the same history it always did; it only lets a recycled book resume instead of replaying), but the chain from the published lineage still carries PR #6's citation/ibid resolution and PR #5's line markers; run a full relink.

Otzaria/otzaria#2408: relative citations naming the citing tractate ("לקמן גיטין דף כג:") are recovered from failed resolutions, and so are untitled ones inside a Bavli tractate or its "X on <tractate>" commentary whose whole anchor is one address ("לקמן יא:", "לעיל ב,א", "לקמן צה ע\"ב", or a lone "לקמן ע\"ב" for the other amud of the citing daf), kept out of the ibid history; lines of a non-Sefaria "X על <tractate>" are placed for this by their own daf headings; output-affecting, run a full relink. Full-book planning is limited by the shared canonical Bavli-title gate, excluding Sefaria and KSK; other books retain exact per-line reuse. Otzaria/otzaria#2490: a failed citation whose parts before its one "(" only locate the address (RELATIVE, or a chapter locator such as "בריש מרובה" / "בפרק החובל") is resolved from the parenthesized title and number alone, kept out of the ibid history; a whole-daf target whose anchor is followed mid-line by ":" right after the spelled daf number becomes amud b. A failed "פרק X דמסכת דף N" (chapter before title, e.g. "בפרק שני דכתובות (דף יח:", "פ"ק דיומא דף י"ד") resolves its title and address alone and is kept only when a chapter it names, in Sefaria's own chapter terms, overlaps the result; the citation is where daf and chapter meet: a whole daf with one amud in the chapter narrows to it, and an amud written after it (":", ".", ע"א/ע"ב) outside the chapter drops the citation. A chapter phrase before a parenthesized address only narrows it the same way and never drops it, since authors use some chapter names for other chapters than Sefaria ("דיני ממונות בתרא" for "זה בורר"). A mid-line colon after spaces or HTML tags also marks amud b; the original anchor extends through that colon, while the spelled-daf and line-final-colon guards still apply. This is output-affecting and requires a full relink. Failed citations whose numbers carry a geresh after more than one letter ("תהלים יח' לא'") are rebuilt from the text when the Ref is a non-empty Tanakh ref with exactly the spelled sections, also kept out of the ibid history. Mixed numeral styles are also recovered: the other number may use standard gershayim, Unicode double quotes or two apostrophes; canonical spelling, exact sections, Tanakh and non-empty checks still apply. PR #10 recovery takes precedence, and both recovery paths stay out of ibid history.

Otzaria/otzaria#3450, #3453: three recoveries of citations Sefaria drops, all kept out of the ibid history; output-affecting, run a full relink. (1) A relative citation whose address opens a parenthesis ("לעיל (דף לו:)") is rebuilt like "לעיל דף לו:", and so is one framed by a chapter ("בספ\"ב (לקמן דף יט:)", "לקמן בפירקין (דף ה.)") when that chapter is the line's own or one of the tractate's own chapters in Sefaria's terms and contains the address. (2) An untitled daf ("(דף כא.)", "התם (דף כז.)") in a Bavli tractate or its "X on <tractate>" commentary links to the tractate's own amud only when every Sefaria candidate is that amud in the tractate or a commentary on it, the anchor ends with it and names no side, the clause before it names no other tractate nor a chapter without it, and an ibid or adjacent preceding citation did not fail and lies in the tractate. (3) A failed citation whose lead words the NER joined to a parenthesized verse or Bavli daf ("בנדה (ויקרא טו יט)") is resolved from the parenthesis alone when every lead word is a plain word, a chapter of the target's book that contains it, or whole titles of works unrelated to the target and of another category unless such a chapter places it; a word that opens a title without completing it ("ירושלמי", "רש\"י") keeps the drop.

PR #13 precision follow-up: require explicit evidence before discarding a lead or converting a commentary target to its Bavli base; validate chapter locators and examine the whole bounded clause. Recover explicit comma-separated Bible addresses independently, and recover addressed ibid references only from the immediately preceding validated citation; Bible inheritance also requires four adjoining words unique in the cited book. Persist preceding-citation state across transport batches and checkpoints (schema 4), leaving Sefaria and legacy emitted-ref history unchanged. Output-affecting; full relink required.
